memory_candidates.content: In this repo's extension system, MCP server REGISTRATION and PERMISSION are two fully independent axes with different owners. Registration happens ONLY in user-scope ~/.claude.json (via a host-level/home-manager activation block or a core/scripts/ setup script, e.g. setup-lean-mcp.sh). An mcpServers key inside settings.json/settings.local.json -- and therefore inside any extension's settings-fragment.json -- is completely inert; Claude Code never reads those files for server definitions. Permission (mcp__{server}__* grants) DOES belong in settings-fragment.json, scoped by domain: extension-specific grants in the owning extension's own fragment, domain-agnostic grants only in core's root-files/settings.json. A settings-declared server shows up nowhere in `claude mcp list` (absent, not failing-to-connect) -- that absence is the diagnostic tell. See agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/mcp-server-ownership.md for the full writeup.

Prefer a single wildcard MCP permission grant ("mcp__{server}__*") over enumerating each tool by name in permissions.allow. An enumeration silently under-grants as the server adds tools over time -- a missed update reintroduces prompting for the new tool with no error signal. This repo's lean-lsp permission drifted to a stale 21-entry enumeration (missing newer tools) duplicated across two files before being collapsed to one wildcard in the owning extension's own settings-fragment.json.

When a documentation/meta task edits only agent-system/extensions/** (the source store) without redeploying, check-extension-docs.sh will report 'deployed script/doc content drift (deployed != extension source)' for every touched file that has a deployed .claude/** counterpart. This is expected and non-blocking, not a defect -- the source-store/deploy boundary rule (.claude/rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md) means .claude/** is a disposable, manually-regenerated artifact. Triage check-extension-docs.sh output by confirming every FAIL/WARN traces either to files this task touched (expected drift, safe to ignore pre-regeneration) or predates the task entirely (unrelated, out of scope) -- never treat source-vs-deployed drift itself as something to fix without a redeploy.
